speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are a neonate presenting with seizures, lethargy, and other neurological signs three days after birth. To determine the cause, I need to ask you a few questions about your birth history and current symptoms. First, was your birth complicated, and did you have any infections like Group B Strep or herpes before delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; your low birth weight, history of chorioamnionitis, and low Apgar scores are significant risk factors. Given the seizures and lethargy, I need to confirm if there are any maternal risk factors like diabetes or substance use, and whether the infant has been feeding well. REQUEST TEST: Blood_glucose, CBC_with_diff, and Serum_electrolytes.

speaker: Doctor
text: The recent blood glucose, CBC, and electrolyte results are within normal limits, so metabolic causes have been ruled out. Given your history of chorioamnionitis, low birth weight, and hypoxia, I need to know if you have a fever or if there are any focal neurological signs like bulging fontanelle or abnormal muscle tone. REQUEST IMAGES: Cranial_CT_scan.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds. I also have Increasing lethargy over the past 18 hours, Appears ill.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Sepsis (likely Group B Streptococcus) with associated Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy.
